h: A Victorian inventor rides forward hundreds of thousands of years and finds a gentle, decayed humanity; short, eerie and sharper about class than it looks.

like.r: Another early vision of a future split into the comfortable and the laboring, with the same dread about where inequality leads.
Time travel as a coping mechanism rather than a gadget, funnier and more wounded than Wells's cool parable.
Another short, sweeping speculation about humanity's fate that trades adventure for awe.

h: Tripod invaders flatten Victorian England in one witness's account; the original alien invasion, with a pointed jab at the arrogance of empire.

like.r: Another very English catastrophe seen by an ordinary survivor, quieter and more domestic than Wells's martial panic.
A modern retelling that keeps the dread and the helpless-witness viewpoint but moves it to a frightened American father.
Humanity meets a vastly superior intelligence, but through slow puzzle-box science rather than sudden machines.

h: A shipwrecked man lands on an island where a surgeon is remaking animals into people; short, feverish and still unpleasantly relevant.

like.r: The ancestor of every mad-scientist story, with the same question of what a creator owes his creation.
A narrator drifts toward a remote domain of one man's unchecked will, with the same dread of civilization peeling away.
Also asks what is done to beings made for a purpose, though it is gentle, restrained and heartbreaking instead of gothic.

t: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
h: A scientist is taken aboard Captain Nemo's submarine for a tour of the ocean floor, part wonder-cabinet, part brooding portrait of a vengeful recluse.

like.r: Another obsessive captain and a ship as a closed world, far denser and more digressive than Verne's brisk travelogue.
The same boyish sea-adventure momentum, with pirates instead of marine science.

like.t: Journey to the Center of the Earth
like.r: Verne's other great expedition into an unexplored world, more cave-crawling and dinosaurs, less moral gloom.

t: Journey to the Center of the Earth
h: A grumpy professor, his nervous nephew and an Icelandic guide descend through a volcano into a prehistoric underworld; pure lost-world fun.

like.r: The same thrill of finding living prehistory, rewritten as a modern techno-thriller.
Another classic boy's-eye quest with brisk pacing and colorful companions.
A shorter, bleaker trip into the unknown, trading Verne's cheerful geology for social warning.

h: A young scientist makes a living creature and flees from it; told in nested confessions, it is sadder and far more eloquent than its screen monsters.

like.r: Another gothic classic told through documents, but with an outside predator rather than a creation haunting its maker.

like.t: The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
like.r: A shorter, sharper tale of a scientist who unleashes something he cannot control.
A modern look at manufactured people and their makers, told with quiet horror instead of lightning and gloom.

h: A mathematician predicts the fall of a galactic empire and sets up a lifeboat civilization; a story about ideas and statecraft, told in talky, clever episodes.

like.r: Another galaxy-spanning story of politics and prophecy, with more atmosphere and a hero in the center.
A far-future human empire seen through linked stories, richer in prose and darker in mood.
Another strategy-minded classic where brains and manipulation matter more than blasters.

h: Nine linked stories about robots bound by three laws and the logic puzzles those laws create; clean, clever thought experiments with a human heart.

like.t: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
like.r: Takes the question of machine minds into noir and paranoia, asking whether it is empathy that sets us apart.
A tight, modern puzzle about a created mind that is more cunning than its creator.
A robot narrator who is more tender than rule-bound, and an emotional rather than logical test of the same idea.

h: Silent alien overlords bring peace and plenty to Earth, and humanity must live with what that costs; a short, awe-struck ride of big questions.

like.r: Clarke's other meditation on humanity's next stage, more visual and enigmatic.
A thoughtful encounter between humans and a different kind of society, more emotional and character-centered.
Another aliens-arrive story that cares about what contact does to our sense of time, meaning and ourselves.

h: From the first tools to a haunted trip past Jupiter with a calm, lying computer; plain, precise prose carries a leap into the unexplainable.

like.r: The film written in tandem with the book is wordless where the novel explains, and endlessly debated.
A silent alien artifact and another exploration of the unknown, handled with the same patient engineering curiosity.
Another meditative encounter with a mind beyond human comprehension, more emotional and dreamlike.

h: A giant, silent cylinder drifts through the solar system and a crew has days to explore it; a rare book where the mystery is the architecture.

like.r: A modern problem-solving space adventure with a warm heart and an equally satisfying alien riddle.
Another story about incomprehensible alien leftovers, with desperate scavengers instead of careful explorers.
A grander engineered megastructure to explore, with more swagger and creature design.

h: A human raised by Martians returns to Earth and starts a new religion; a talky, countercultural satire that is both charming and uncomfortable.

like.t: The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress
like.r: Heinlein's other classic, more political and plot-driven, about a revolution run by a witty computer.
Another counterculture-era novel about an outsider, wittier and sadder, with sex and religion treated as absurdity.
Also turns a messiah figure into a warning, in a far more detailed and fatalistic world.

h: A recruit in powered armor fights an insectoid enemy and absorbs a philosophy of duty; a brisk, argumentative military story.

like.r: A Vietnam-veteran answer to Heinlein, bitterly questioning the same kind of war.
The film turns the book's sincere militarism into outrageous satire.
Another young soldier trained for an alien war, with more psychology and a nastier cost.

t: The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress
h: Lunar convicts and a self-aware computer plot a revolution against Earth, in a slangy first-person voice that makes politics feel like a caper.

like.r: Heinlein's more philosophical, countercultural side, with sermons and free love in place of revolution.
Another wry, engineering-minded survival story that treats every problem as a puzzle to be hacked.
Another story of a harsh world rising against distant masters, grander and more mystical.

h: A fireman who burns books starts to read them; a short, lyrical alarm about screens, noise and the quiet loss of attention.

like.r: The grimmer, more political dystopia about controlled information and language.
Shows society controlled by pleasure and distraction rather than fire, closer to Bradbury's worry.
Another near-future state that polices what can be read and said, told with a more intimate, personal voice.

h: Linked stories of settlers reaching Mars and what they bring with them; more a mournful small-town American elegy than rocket science.

like.r: Bradbury's darker autumn fantasy, with the same lyrical nostalgia.
Another classic that uses a far-flung future to watch civilization repeat itself, with a strong sorrow in it.
A humane, anthropological look at an alien culture instead of a conquest.

h: A duke's heir is thrown into a desert planet where spice, religion and ecology decide empires; dense, political and deeply planned.

like.r: The first half of the story onscreen, with a visual scale that matches the book's atmosphere.
Another ornate far-future epic with religion and politics in the mix, told through multiple narrators.
Another galactic-empire saga about prediction and power, more intellectual and with less mysticism.

t: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
h: A bounty hunter retires rebel androids in a ruined world where owning a living animal means status; about empathy more than about gunplay.

like.r: The famous adaptation keeps the hunt but swaps the book's animal obsession for neon noir.
Another neon-lit future of fake and real minds, more digital and stylish.
Dick at his most reality-melting and funny-paranoid.

t: The Man in the High Castle
h: Americans live under Axis occupation, and a banned novel imagines a different outcome; quiet, eerie and about what makes anything authentic.

like.r: A fuller portrait of total control, harsher and more political than Dick's oblique version.
Another regime-in-America nightmare told through ordinary people trying to get by.
Dick at his most reality-melting, with the same doubt about what is real.

h: Psychics, a dead boss and a world that keeps reverting to the past; a short, funny-paranoid novel where reality itself is the con.

like.r: Dick's more somber, personal take on a mind coming apart.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: A mind-bending story of memory and reality that is as strange as Ubik but warmer.

like.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
like.r: A different kind of comic absurdity in SF, sunnier and more silly.

h: An undercover narcotics agent is assigned to spy on himself while sinking into the drug he is investigating; funny at first, then devastating.

like.r: The rotoscoped adaptation is faithful to the book's paranoid humor and sadness.

like.t: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
like.r: Dick's more famous take on a mind unsure of what is real, with a clearer plot.
Another vast, dark-funny book on addiction, much larger and more maximalist.

h: An envoy visits a frozen world whose people have no fixed gender and slowly forms a deep bond with its prime minister; patient, humane and moving.

like.r: Le Guin's other landmark, about politics, anarchism and a physicist caught between two worlds.
Another thoughtful social SF by a major woman author, grittier and nearer to now.
A modern space opera that plays with gender and identity, with a faster, more political plot.

h: A physicist leaves a poor, stateless moon for its rich rival planet; a patient novel that weighs freedom, property and what a utopia costs.

like.r: Le Guin's more intimate, wintry story of friendship across a cultural divide.
Another novel that treats building a new society as a political and scientific argument.
A flipside look at engineered society, bleaker and more satirical.

h: A psychologist arrives at a station orbiting an ocean-planet that reads minds and returns dead loved ones; contact stripped of answers.

like.r: A long, haunted adaptation that turns the novel's grief into pure mood.
Another expedition to a place that resists understanding, in a wetter, creepier register.
A Soviet-era sibling about incomprehensible alien traces, rougher and more street-level.

h: Stalkers sneak into a fenced Zone full of deadly alien leftovers to sell what they find; a weary, sardonic tale of a town living off a miracle.

like.r: Tarkovsky's slow, philosophical film loosely based on the novel strips the plot down to a spiritual walk.
Another journey into a changed zone no one can explain, dreamier and more biological.
Another classic about the limits of understanding an alien intelligence.

h: A bombing survivor comes unstuck in time and drifts between a prison camp, a marriage and an alien zoo; funny on the surface and wrecked beneath.

like.r: Another dark-comic war novel with a nonlinear structure and a circular logic of absurdity.
Vonnegut's other great satirical SF, lighter on trauma and more about belief and doom.

like.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
like.r: Comic SF that uses the same deadpan to keep the universe's cruelty at arm's length.

h: A writer researching the atomic bomb's inventor ends up on a Caribbean island with a made-up religion; short, jokey, bleak and unforgettable.

like.r: The more famous and more personal Vonnegut, built around war trauma instead of invented religion.
Another black comedy that laughs at the apocalypse and the men who might bring it.
Another satire where institutions are mad and everyone is trapped in a joke with no exit.

h: Told through a man's progress reports, a lab experiment turns a gentle man with a low IQ into a genius, then shows what it costs; a gut-punch of a book.

like.r: Another quiet SF story about a person shaped by science, equally heartbreaking and restrained.
The older story of a scientist's overreach and a creation that wants to be loved.
A similarly short and tender story about a gentle man and the cruelty of the world around him.

h: Monks in the American desert preserve scraps of knowledge across centuries after nuclear war; wry, learned and wary that history may repeat.

like.r: A starker, more intimate view of the ashes, with no monastic humor.
A gentler post-collapse tale of people carrying culture through the dark.
Another richly learned novel set among monks and manuscripts.

h: Most of humanity wakes up blind just as walking, stinging plants run loose; a sober English cosy catastrophe with a lean survivalist edge.

like.r: A film that borrows the empty-London opening and carries it into a more violent nightmare.
The older English apocalypse seen through one witness, with a more rampaging threat.
A modern take on a vanished world and the small communities that outlast it, gentler and more lyrical.

h: A crew crash-lands on a giant artificial ring around a star; a rambling hard-SF expedition in which the setting is the star.

like.r: A similar enormous alien structure to explore, more reserved and mysterious.
A bigger and more mythic rendition of strange worlds shaping characters.

like.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
like.r: A comic cousin with just as many wild galactic ideas, played for laughs.

h: A modern Black woman keeps being pulled back to a Maryland plantation; a brutal, intimate time-travel novel where history is something you endure.

like.r: Another haunting novel of slavery's aftermath, more lyrical and ghostly.
Butler's near-future survival story with the same clear-eyed look at violence.
Another speculative reimagining of slavery's America, more panoramic and episodic.

h: A young woman with hyper-empathy keeps a journal as California collapses and invents a new faith while walking north; grim, urgent and plainspoken.

like.r: A bleaker road trip through ruin, with less hope and a sparer voice.
Another near-future American collapse seen through a woman's private account.
A warmer, more elegiac post-collapse story about carrying something precious across a ruined land.

h: After nuclear war, a woman is woken by tentacled aliens who offer survival at the price of merging with them; a tense study of consent and coercion.

like.r: Butler's most-read novel is about another unequal, coercive bond, grounded in real history.
Another strange contact story where change to the body is unavoidable and ambiguous.
Another first-contact classic about gender and cultural difference, calmer and more sympathetic.

h: A burned-out hacker is hired for one last run into cyberspace; a hard-boiled caper that gave the future its neon vocabulary.

like.r: The visual twin of Gibson's rain-slicked future, though moodier and more about memory.
A funnier, faster cyberpunk romp with the same appetite for technology and a lot more jokes.
Takes cyberspace and hacker mythology into a blockbuster with kung fu.

h: A pizza-delivering hacker named Hiro Protagonist chases a virus that works on brains as well as computers; cyberpunk played as a manic satire.

like.r: The moodier, more stylized ancestor of the genre this book is joking about.
A lighter, pop-culture-stuffed virtual-world adventure with a more earnest hero.
Both treat a digital world as a place to fight, with a more serious tone in the film.

h: A shape-changing mercenary hunts a runaway machine mind in the middle of a galactic war; inventive, bloody and sardonic space opera.

like.r: Another sprawling far-future epic of war and gods, more structured around linked tales.
A grittier, closer-to-home space adventure with the same appetite for plot and politics.
The older benchmark for sweeping, politically dense SF, with a prophecy in place of Banks's cynicism.

h: Seven pilgrims tell their stories on the way to a time-twisting killer; a Canterbury Tales in space with horror, romance and detective fiction inside.

like.r: Another dense, ornate saga of faith and empire, told as a single epic.
Another nested book of tales in different genres, trading space opera for a chain across centuries.
A darker, more streetwise view of a future of AIs and sprawling networks.

h: A gifted child is raised in an orbital war school to defend Earth from aliens; a fast, manipulative story about what we do to kids for victory.

like.r: Another story of children trained and used for violence, with a more romantic and political edge.
The earlier military-training SF that this answers, more didactic and less interested in the soldiers' feelings.
A bitter look at fighting an interstellar war, for adults and more about alienation than strategy.

h: A soldier fights across the stars while relativity ensures that home moves centuries ahead; a Vietnam-era war novel in dress uniform.

like.r: The pro-military novel this was written against, with a similar training-to-battle shape.
A lighter, funnier take on the same older-soldiers-in-space idea.
Another story that makes time dilation a source of heartbreak.

h: A galaxy where physics changes with distance and a loosed superintelligence races a rescue; includes some of SF's best alien pack-minds.

like.r: Another novel that makes alien minds deeply believable, with spiders instead of dog-packs.
A lusher, more literary far-future epic with a looming godlike threat.
Another big-canvas space opera, with more wit and less physics.

h: An Oxford historian is sent back to the Middle Ages just as a plague hits the future she left; a humane, painful and absorbing time-travel novel.

like.r: A romance-driven time-slip into an earlier Britain, longer and more adventurous.
Another epidemic novel with compassion and a shifting timeline.
Another time traveler stuck in a hostile past, harsher and more personal.

t: To Say Nothing of the Dog
h: A time-lagged historian is sent to Victorian England on a society-saving errand; a comedy of manners with cats, rowing and a lot of chaos.

like.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
like.r: Another very English SF comedy, sillier and more cosmic.
The Victorian river comedy that Willis openly loves and borrows from.
The author's grimmer companion piece in the same world of time travel.

h: In a theocratic America, a woman valued only for her fertility remembers what came before; a cold, controlled voice makes it more chilling.

like.r: The foundational total-control dystopia, with surveillance in place of control of the body.
Reverses the gender hierarchy to look at power from the other side, faster and more lurid.
Another quiet, first-person look at the horrors of a system, with the same unemphatic voice.

h: The last man alive among gentle engineered people recalls how his brilliant friend ended the world; satirical, mournful and eerily plausible.

like.r: Atwood's best-known dystopia is more political and less about biotech.
Another novel that splits time between the collapse and what follows, though warmer.
A classic about a society shaped by biotechnology and pleasure.

h: Three friends grow up at an English boarding school and slowly understand what they are for; calm, nostalgic and devastating.

like.r: A faithful, hushed adaptation with the same restrained heartbreak.
Ishiguro's other great study of a narrator who hides from his own life, in a country-house setting.
A shorter story of science used on a person, told in a simpler and more direct voice.

h: A father and son walk through a burned, cannibal-haunted America toward the sea; very bleak, very short on words, and one of the most tender books about love.

like.r: A grim, faithful film of the book, ashes and fear in every frame.
Another post-collapse novel, much warmer and more hopeful about art.
McCarthy's earlier masterwork of violence, in a western landscape and denser prose.

h: During China's Cultural Revolution a scientist's message goes to the stars, and decades later physicists begin to die; hard SF on a huge scale.

like.r: Another case where humanity meets a huge alien enigma, calmer and less dark about it.
A warmer, funnier science-puzzle novel about a cosmic crisis.
A film about first contact as a problem of communication, more emotional and humane.

h: An astronaut left for dead on Mars solves one lethal problem after another with duct tape, chemistry and wisecracks; a delight for puzzle fans.

like.r: A breezy, faithful adaptation that keeps the humor and the can-do science.
Weir's second novel keeps the problem-solving and adds a friendship that is something special.
A true-story drama of people solving impossible space problems with improvisation.

h: The last body of a destroyed starship's mind hunts the ruler who ordered its death; a cool revenge story that plays with gender, grammar and empire.

like.r: The classic that first made gender a science-fictional question.
Another artificial narrator with an odd, deadpan view of humans, in a lighter and shorter package.
Another space opera about machines and empires, with more swagger.

t: The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet
h: A patched-together crew punches a wormhole through space; a comfort-food space opera about the people on the ship instead of the war outside.

like.r: A cozier-than-it-looks short space adventure with a lovably grumpy narrator.
The original found-family space adventure, with more swashbuckling and less introspection.

like.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
like.r: An old favorite that shares the sense of a big, odd, friendly galaxy.

h: A security android who has hacked its own governor module would rather watch soap operas than guard scientists, until something attacks; short, funny, sneakily moving.

like.r: Another inhuman narrator in a space opera, colder and more political.

like.t: The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet
like.r: A comforting space story about a crew of misfits, with less action and more feelings.

like.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
like.r: A comic space romp in which a robot is among the best characters.

h: The last humans search for a home as a terraformed planet's spiders evolve culture below; two societies converge, one gloriously alien.

like.r: Another novel in which very alien minds drive the story, with a more far-flung galaxy.
Another story where an unlikely alien friendship carries the plot, sunnier and quicker.
Another long, ecologically minded saga about how a species adapts to a harsh world.

t: Stories of Your Life and Others
h: Eight precise stories, each built on one strange idea, from a Tower of Babel to a linguist learning an alien tongue; thought-provoking and emotionally clear.

like.r: The film of the title story, which keeps the way language, time and grief fold into each other.
Another humane, idea-driven SF classic about understanding someone very different.
Classic puzzle-box SF stories, more mechanical and less spiritual.

h: After a flu wipes out most of the world, a troupe of actors tours the ruins, performing Shakespeare; elegiac and quietly hopeful.

like.r: A harsher, barer way through the same ruined world, with no theater.
Another post-collapse novel that asks what we should save, with monks instead of actors.
A similar braided structure across time, more experimental and more playful.

h: A biologist joins an expedition into a coastal zone where nature is rewriting itself; a short, wet, dreamlike descent into dread.

like.r: A looser, more visual adaptation that keeps the dread and shimmering strangeness.
The classic zone story that made this kind of quest what it is.
Another encounter with something that will not be understood, colder and more philosophical.

h: A Chicago physics professor is kidnapped, wakes up in a life that is not his and must find his way home; a chase through multiple worlds.

like.r: Another multiverse story about the other lives we might have had, wilder and funnier.
Crouch's next high-concept thriller, the same speed with memory and time as the engine.
A twisty heist through layers of reality driven by a man's desire to get home to his family.

h: A detective and a neuroscientist chase a memory disease that rewrites people's pasts; a breakneck thriller with a mind-bending, heartfelt core.

like.r: Crouch's earlier, more personal chase through alternate lives, also at top speed.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: Another story about what editing memory does to love, quieter and more tender.
A romance driven by time's tangles, much more emotional and less plot-heavy.

h: At seventy-five, a widower joins an interstellar army that promises him a young body; brisk, sarcastic and good-hearted military SF.

like.r: The older classic that Scalzi talks back to, more solemn and political.
Bleaker and more antiwar, with the same long-distance soldier's alienation.

like.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
like.r: A comic-space book with the same quick banter and a more absurd bent.

h: A weary detective and a ship's officer stumble on a conspiracy that could ignite a war between Earth, Mars and the Belt; noir meets space.

like.r: Another space opera with grit and scale, though less grounded in physics.
Another near-solar-system saga of colonies and politics, slower and more scientific.
A grimy, working-class vision of space travel with a horror edge.

h: A glass city runs on mathematics and nobody is ever alone; a diary of an engineer who falls in love, and the ancestor of the modern dystopia.

like.r: Directly inspired by We, and just as bleak, though more brutal and closer to politics.
Another early dystopia of engineered conformity, more satirical and sensuous.
A film from the same decade with a similarly mechanized, class-split future city.

h: A world of engineered castes, easy pleasure and a drug called soma meets a savage who has read Shakespeare; a dystopia of comfort.

like.r: The opposite nightmare: control by pain and fear instead of pleasure.
A shorter, warmer-hearted warning about a society numbed by entertainment.
A modern, darkly funny story about biotech, consumerism and what they do to humanity.

h: A clerk who rewrites the past for the Party risks a love affair and a diary; the original blueprint for the surveillance state, and still deeply unnerving.

like.r: Its pleasure-based counterpart, where control comes through comfort and not terror.
Brings the same totalitarian dread into a personal and gendered frame.
A darkly comic film about a faceless bureaucracy and a little man's dreams.

t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
h: The Earth is demolished for a bypass and one bewildered Englishman hitches a ride across the stars; wonderfully silly and endlessly quotable.

like.r: Another very English comedy about the end of the world, with angels and demons in the lead.
A darker satire with a similar shrug at cosmic absurdity.
A modern space comedy with a gloomy, funny narrator that Marvin would enjoy.

h: A man wakes alone on a spaceship with no memory and a world to save; science problem-solving and one of the most lovable friendships in the genre.

like.r: Weir's first book, with the same engineering-as-adventure fun and a stranded hero.
A bigger and weepier film about saving humanity from space with a father's sacrifice.
Another novel that makes an alien species feel real, with a longer and more epic scope.

h: The first hundred settlers begin to terraform Mars and split over whether they should; a meticulous saga of geology, politics and colonial argument.

like.r: A more compact novel on building a new society, with a stronger emotional pull.
A lighter, faster story that has the same love of Martian engineering detail.
A pacier thriller about the politics of solar-system colonization.

h: A strange moment of music and a glitch in the air connect an exile, a composer, a novelist and a time investigator; a quiet puzzle about being alive.

like.r: The author's best-known book also moves between eras and finds hope in art.
Another novel that links lives across centuries, bolder in formal play.
Another mild, thoughtful SF novel that feels more like literary fiction.

h: A solar-powered artificial friend watches the human family who might choose her; a hushed, naive narrator reveals more than she understands.

like.r: Ishiguro's earlier, bleaker novel about a made being and its fate.
The classic story set that treats robots as ethical puzzles, more cerebral and less moving.
Another gentle story of a human attachment to an artificial mind.

h: Teenage girls discover they can deliver electric shocks, and the world's balance of power flips; a provocative, brutal thought experiment.

like.r: The classic gender-power dystopia, colder and from the other side.
Another novel about how violent societies remake themselves, with a quieter, spiritual center.
A cooler satirical dystopia about what happens when technology outruns ethics.

h: A crew of modified humans and a vampire go to meet a silent alien ship; chilling hard SF about consciousness that few novels dare to ask.

like.r: The classic book of an alien mind beyond our comprehension, with more melancholy and less biology.
Another unsettling expedition into the incomprehensible, written in a more dreamlike key.
Hard SF with a similarly pessimistic view of what the universe holds.

h: A radio astronomer picks up a signal from Vega and the world must decide how to answer; a hopeful novel about science, belief and awe.

like.r: The well-loved film adaptation with Jodie Foster, which sharpens the faith and science argument.
A similar sense of cosmic wonder, with more engineering and less belief.

like.t: Stories of Your Life and Others
like.r: A collection with a similarly thoughtful, humane sense of what contact would mean.

h: Cloned dinosaurs, an island theme park and a security system that fails; a page-turner of chaos theory and corporate arrogance.

like.r: The classic movie keeps the set pieces and loses the book's lectures and some grisly bits.
The first novel of science creating what it cannot control.
Another science-dense thriller that makes problem-solving feel like action.

h: Six nested stories in different genres and centuries, from a Pacific diary to a post-human future, echo each other; ambitious, showy and unexpectedly warm.

like.c: Lana Wachowski, Tom Tykwer & Lilly Wachowski
like.r: A daring film version that links the stories by casting the same actors across eras.
A smaller and more focused novel that also threads people across time.
Another nested set of stories across genres, with a more classic SF payoff.

h: A Jesuit mission goes to meet the singers of a distant planet; told through the sole survivor's ruin, it is a tragedy about faith, friendship and hubris.

like.r: Another first-contact classic that ends in sorrow, but with a more alien mystery.
Another SF novel where faith and the Church sit at the center.
A more hopeful treatment of the encounter with an alien that centers a very human grief.

h: In a decaying future, a teenager hunts for a dead billionaire's hidden prize inside a virtual world built from 1980s pop culture; a nostalgic quest.

like.r: The sharper, funnier ancestor of the virtual-world adventure.
Another story of a gamer kid being asked to save the world, grimmer and more serious.
A pop-culture touchstone with the same 80s adventure spirit.

h: A solicitor's visit to a Transylvanian castle sets off a hunt across England, told in diaries and telegrams; the template for every vampire since.

like.r: A lush, romantic and bloody adaptation that adds a love story to Stoker's fear of the outsider.
Another gothic classic told through documents, centered on a creator and his creation.
Turns the vampire inside out, giving the monster the voice and the sorrow.

h: A lonely girl in an Austrian castle befriends a mysterious guest; the short, sensual vampire novella that came first and outsmarts Dracula.

like.r: The grander, more famous vampire novel that this one preceded and helped inspire.
Another short, ambiguous Victorian gothic about a female narrator and an unsettling presence.
A modern heir of gothic atmosphere, with a decaying house and a heroine who fights back.

t: The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
h: A lawyer pieces together the link between a respectable doctor and a violent brute; a short, foggy London mystery with a moral sting.

like.r: Another Victorian story of a respectable face hiding something rotten, more decadent and witty.
The earlier scientific-hubris gothic, longer and more eloquent.
Brings the double-self theme into a modern horror classic.

h: A beautiful young man stays unlined while his portrait ages with his sins; decadent, epigram-packed and ultimately moral.

like.t: The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
like.r: A shorter, plot-driven Victorian tale of a man and the self he hides.
Another decadent gothic classic in which fear of the hidden life is key.
A modern story of beautiful, aesthetic young people and the guilt they hide.

h: A governess becomes sure the two children in her charge are haunted by ghosts; whether it is real or in her head is the whole game.

like.r: A cool, eerie adaptation that keeps the book's ambiguity.
Another haunted-house story in which the heroine's mind is as unsettled as the building.
Another young woman in a house ruled by a presence from the past, more romantic and plot-driven.

h: Four people spend a summer in a house with a bad reputation, and the lonely one starts to belong; fear built from a sentence at a time.

like.r: The classic black-and-white adaptation, one of the creepiest haunted house films ever.

like.t: We Have Always Lived in the Castle
like.r: Jackson's other masterpiece, wittier and more about an eccentric family than ghosts.
The older, more ambiguous ghost story that Jackson built on.

t: We Have Always Lived in the Castle
h: Two sisters and an uncle live in a big house, shunned by the village after a poisoning; narrated by an eighteen-year-old whose voice is a delight and a chill.

like.r: Jackson's ghost story, with the same slow dread and a more fragile heroine.
Another house-centered story of secrets and obsession, more romantic.
A modern gothic where a strange family house is the monster.

h: An Antarctic expedition finds a vast frozen city older than humans; a pulpy, over-written and surprisingly modern tale of dread of deep time.

like.r: A recent expedition into a place that defies understanding, with a more modern, ecological dread.
Another polar base with an unspeakable alien presence, in a film of paranoia and gore.
Another work that makes space itself the horror, now with experimental typography.

h: A nameless second wife arrives at Manderley, a house still ruled by the first; the best lingering-dread opening in English fiction.

like.r: A sleek, shadowy adaptation that holds up well, though it softens one key part of the story.
The classic young-woman-in-a-secret-house novel that du Maurier is answering.
A slow, creeping novel about a decaying English estate and what haunts it.

h: A recovering alcoholic takes a caretaker job at a snowbound hotel with his wife and psychic son; a family drama that curdles into a haunting.

like.r: A cold, formal and iconic film that differs in its bleaker take on the father.
The classic that King openly draws on, all insinuation instead of blood.
Written by King's son, another story about a man and a haunting that follows him.

h: Seven outcast kids and the shape-shifting thing under their Maine town, told in two timelines; a big-hearted, very long monster story about friendship.

like.r: A glossy modern adaptation of the childhood half, with more jump scares and less sprawl.
Another nostalgic coming-of-age novel of small-town childhood and the supernatural.
King's other brick of an epic, with a whole country at risk instead of one town.

h: A doctor moves his family to rural Maine and finds a burial ground that does not keep the dead dead; King's grimmest and most parental horror.

like.r: A campy but nasty adaptation that keeps the book's central horror.
A quieter story that treats grief and family as the real haunting.
Another family unraveling in a New England house, with doubt about what is real.

h: A bullied teenager with a fanatical mother discovers telekinesis; told partly through clippings, it is a compact tragedy of cruelty and rage.

like.r: A stylish film adaptation famous for its prom scene and its final shock.
Another look at female rage and the body, as literary short fiction.
Another cult of a woman controlled by those around her, in a bright domestic setting.

h: A writer returns to his Maine hometown as vampires move in; a slow-spreading rot that gets inside a whole community.

like.r: The inspiration, transplanted by King to a modern American small town.
Another town-level haunting with a literary, layered structure.

like.t: The Southern Book Club's Guide to Slaying Vampires
like.r: A modern, funnier take on vampires in a close-knit community.

h: A famous novelist is rescued from a car wreck by his self-proclaimed number one fan; a two-person nightmare about readers and writers.

like.r: A tight, much-loved adaptation with a famous performance from Kathy Bates.
A classic of obsession and psychological control, in a gothic rather than a modern key.
A more recent psychological thriller about a person who takes control of someone else's story.

h: A flu kills almost everyone, and the survivors drift toward two camps; King's sprawling American apocalypse of dreams, prophets and quiet heroism.

like.r: A far more delicate vision of the post-plague world.
A slower, more learned view of the world after the end.
A leaner, much bleaker plague survival story.

h: A man solves a puzzle box and opens a door to creatures who treat pain as pleasure; a short, feverish novella that mixes desire and mutilation.

like.r: The author's own film turns the novella's grotesque ideas into a cult-horror landmark.
Barker's earlier story collection, more varied and more inventive in its horror.
Another take on bodies, desire and horror, more literary and political.

h: Short stories that treat the horror as a place of weird beauty, from a slaughterhouse to a London cellar; vivid, gory, wildly imaginative.

like.r: A modern collection that finds literary edges in the body and in fear.
A single, concentrated shot of Barker's extreme gothic.
An older weird-fiction foundation, more cosmic and with less flesh.

h: Four old men tell ghost stories and share a buried crime, and a thing from their past comes back to their New York town; layered and literate.

like.r: A more straightforward and popular town-under-siege story.
A shorter and more restrained ghost story with a similar literary touch.
The classic of ambiguous ghosts that Straub was in conversation with.

h: A vampire tells a reporter his life from plantation Louisiana to Paris; lush, sensuous and lonely, with a monster who hates being one.

like.r: A starry, velvet-draped film of the book, a little shallower but still seductive.
The vampire as predator, in a story that makes Rice's sympathetic monster feel new.
A lushly written, more scholarly vampire quest across Europe.

h: The last man in a plague-stricken Los Angeles fights vampire-like neighbors by night and grief by day; spare, lonely and with a title that pays off.

like.r: King's epic of a plague-emptied America, bigger and more hopeful.
A bleaker tale of survival and a father's love in an empty world.
A fast, grim film that borrows the plague and empty-city mood.

h: Four investigators spend a week in the most haunted house in the world; a nasty, fast, no-nonsense update of the haunted house formula.

like.r: The more subtle model for Matheson's tougher, more brutal haunted-house story.
A more character-driven haunting that took the same sense of an evil building.
A more restrained, old-fashioned English ghost tale.

h: A young wife in a Manhattan apartment becomes convinced her neighbors want her baby; a short, gaslighting thriller that makes pregnancy a horror.

like.r: A very faithful adaptation, with Mia Farrow's performance as the dread center.
Another bestseller of domestic evil, with more faith and more gore.
A modern marriage thriller built on trust, doubt and who is lying.

h: A movie star's daughter changes in her Georgetown bedroom and two priests are called; a serious, doubt-ridden novel behind the scare-fest.

like.r: The famous film is more punishing and more visceral than the novel.
A shorter and more sly domestic horror from the same era.
Another horror novel about a parent facing something awful for a child.

h: A family finds their house is bigger inside than out; footnotes, unusual layouts and an unreliable annotator turn a haunted house into a puzzle.

like.r: The restrained original of a house that seems to think.
Another massive, footnote-heavy cult novel that demands patience.
A shorter story about a space that does not obey the rules, with a similar dread.

h: An aging rock star buys a ghost online and it arrives in a black suit; a fast road-trip horror novel with a heavy-metal swagger.

like.r: By Hill's father: another damaged man pursued by a haunting.
A denser and more literary ghost novel about old crimes coming back.
Another quick, high-concept horror novel whose pressure never lets up.

t: The Cabin at the End of the World
h: Four strangers with homemade weapons arrive at a family's lakeside cabin and say the world ends unless one of them chooses; a hostage thriller of belief.

like.r: Tremblay's earlier horror, also ambiguous about what is real.
A tight, contained apocalypse horror, with a mother making impossible choices.
A modern horror film with a similar single-setting tension and social bite.

h: A girl recalls how her sister's possible possession became a reality TV show; a smart, self-aware horror novel about belief, media and doubt.

like.r: The classic of possession in a family home, with less doubt and more spectacle.

like.t: We Have Always Lived in the Castle
like.r: Another story of a strange family narrated by a young girl.
Another horror novel that plays with the way it is told.

h: A glamorous socialite visits her cousin's husband's rotting house in the Mexican mountains; mold, secrets and a heroine who will not be quiet.

like.r: The classic bride-in-a-haunted-house story that this updates with a sharper sense of power.
Another novel in which the house itself is alive and hungry.
A lush gothic film with a similar decaying mansion and sinister family.

t: How to Sell a Haunted House
h: Two estranged siblings clear out their dead parents' house and its angry puppet; a sibling comedy first, a haunted house story second, with real grief.

like.t: The Southern Book Club's Guide to Slaying Vampires
like.r: Hendrix's other crowd-pleaser, in a Southern neighborhood with a monster.
Another family-and-grief horror novel, much bleaker.
Another funny take on the supernatural that never loses its heart.

t: The Southern Book Club's Guide to Slaying Vampires
h: A Charleston housewife book club realizes the charming new neighbor is a monster; domestic comedy with a fearsome, bloody underside.

like.r: The grandfather of small-town vampire stories, with a more serious tone.
Another vampire story set in the South, glossy and gloomy where Hendrix is funny.
The original vampire hunt, in which a group of friends fights the monster.

h: Eight stories turn women's bodies, desire and fear into folk tales and satire; strange, sensual and sharply angry.

like.r: The older master of unease whose women are similarly watched by the places they live.
Another horror collection obsessed with bodies, with more gore and less politics.
Another novel of women's bodies as the front line of power.

h: Something outside drives anyone who sees it to violence, so a mother and two children row blindfolded downriver; high-concept and relentlessly tense.

like.r: Another film about surviving by denying one of your senses, with a parent's love at its center.
A weightier, sparer book about a parent and child on a hard road.

like.t: The Cabin at the End of the World
like.r: Another confined, high-stakes horror novel with an agonizing choice.

h: Two boys and a sinister carnival that rolls into town in October; a lyrical, autumnal fantasy that is a bit scary and a lot wistful.

like.r: Bradbury's other lyrical elegy, using Mars as its small-town backdrop.
A bigger, bloodier tale of boys and an evil that preys on a town.
A gentler, whimsical Gothic coming-of-age.

h: A young solicitor sorts out a dead woman's papers in a house cut off by the tide; a short, traditional English ghost story of real, creeping fear.

like.r: A gloomy, jump-heavy film version that keeps the setting and the tide.
A classic ghost story with a more ambiguous mind at its center.
A longer, more psychological English house story.

h: A country doctor befriends the declining family of a crumbling Warwickshire hall and something begins to stir; a postwar ghost story about class.

like.r: Another English house novel of obsession and dread, more romantic and propulsive.
A shorter story where the haunting could just be in the minds of the people.
A quiet, rainy-day gothic film about a mother, a big house and a slow reveal.
